run.prompt: Draw an animated SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle. Make the wheels turn and the pelican pedal. Respect prefers-reduced-motion.
run.notes: First and only accepted generation; the generator script ran once and the accepted bytes were not modified after being written. Drawing and animation were produced by a Python script written in this session: 24 phase samples per 1.6 s pedal revolution; each leg is a two-bone IK solve (thigh 82, shin 92, crank radius 36, forward knee) baked into per-phase thigh/shin rotation keyframes so both webbed feet track the pedal spindles exactly; pedal groups counter-rotate at the crank rate to stay level; body bob, wing flap, scarf flutter and fish-tail wiggle are baked from the same phase samples so they stay in sync; wheels, chainring and crank arms spin via CSS keyframes; clouds drift and road dashes plus chain runs animate via translateX and stroke-dashoffset; a prefers-reduced-motion media query disables every animation class. Verified in headless Chrome by pinning each CSS animation's currentTime and sampling 9 phases of the revolution: measured foot centroids match the crank orbit at every sampled phase and the pose at 1.6 s returns to the pose at 0 s; the reduced-motion render is byte-identical to the poster. Context is existing-conversation: PELICAN.md, both protocol files, both schemas, the validator and its unit tests, and the manifest were read in this conversation before authoring; the style block of one existing animated submission was inspected to confirm the transform-box/transform-origin convention; no submitted artwork was viewed. Model identity Step-5-Preview is what the system reports and is not independently verified, so model.id is null; provider StepFun is the model's origin, also not independently verified. Known cosmetic defects recorded rather than corrected: the chain runs are animated dashed strokes rather than linked chains; the far and near legs share one screen plane; the hips are fixed and the body bob is cosmetic, so leg IK is solved at fixed hips; the saddle is largely occluded by the body; the fish is static except its tail; beak pouch and body shapes are simplified; each wheel has 8 spokes and completes 1.6 revolutions per pedal revolution.
